Senses.Explanation: Three phrases is a structural label for words arranged as a triad. Chan records fill that form with several genuinely different named sets, including the corpus-wide pattern and the distinct triads associated with Fenyang, Yunmen, and Linji. The form can carry different contents: Wuzhu names recollectionlessness, thoughtlessness, and non-delusion as a three-phrase teaching (無憶 / 無念 / 莫妄), while Zhaozhou tests his interlocutor by saying that his speech remains within the three phrases even when it gets outside them (語話不出得三句裏；然直饒出得也在三句裏). The expression 'outside the three phrases' (三句外, 102 occurrences) also shows the label circulating as a unit. The distinct named sets associated with Fenyang, Yunmen, and Linji have their own senses below.
Senses.Note: A corpus-wide structural sense. The phrase names the triadic form, not one invariant set; the distinct Fenyang, Yunmen, and Linji configurations are separated below.

Occurrences.Kwic: 透過三句外，自然與佛無差，橫行也得、直行也得，無能攔攩；殺也不怕、活也不怕，豈解傷鋒？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Recorded Sayings of Master Shouchang Wuming (壽昌無明和尚語錄), Wuming Huijing says in a small-group address that passing outside the three phrases leaves one unobstructed in either direction.

Occurrences.Kwic: 公問曰弟子聞金和尚說無憶無念莫妄三句法門是否曰然公曰此三句是一是三曰無憶名戒無念名定莫妄名慧一心不生具戒定慧非一非三也
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Jade Flowers Collection of the Transmission of the Lamp (fragment) (傳燈玉英集（殘卷）), Wuzhu answers Du Hongjian's public question about the three phrases attributed to Master Kim and states their named members.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云：「這僧多少時在老僧這裏，作與麼語話不出得三句裏；然直饒出得也在三句裏，你作麼生？」僧云：「某甲使得三句。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Recorded Sayings of Master Zhaozhou (趙州和尚語錄), Zhaozhou Congshen tests a monk by saying that his speech remains within the three phrases even when it gets outside them.

AlternateTargets: the exerting-strength, turning-body, and intimate phrases
Senses.Explanation: The set called Fenyang's three phrases consists of 'the phrase on which a student exerts strength' (學人著力句), 'the phrase by which a student turns the body' (學人轉身句), and 'the intimate phrase for a student' (學人親切句). In a hall address Fenyang answers the three questions in sequence: 'Jiāzhou makes a great image' (嘉州打大像), 'Shǎn Prefecture casts an iron ox' (陝府灌銕牛), and 'West of the River plays with a lion' (西河弄師子). Eye of Humans and Gods preserves the exchange under the explicit heading 'Fenyang's three phrases' (汾陽三句).
Senses.Note: A distinct named triad, separated from the corpus-wide structural sense and from the differently constituted Yunmen and Linji sets. The entry reports the recorded members and answers without assigning them an explanatory meaning.

Occurrences.Kwic: 汾陽三句汾陽三句汾陽上堂僧出問。如何是學人著力句。汾云。嘉州打大像。如何是學人轉身句。汾云。陝府灌銕牛。如何是學人親切句。汾云。西河弄師子。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Eye of Humans and Gods (人天眼目), Fenyang Shanzhao presents Fenyang's three phrases as the exerting-strength, turning-body, and intimate phrases.

Senses.Explanation: The set called Yunmen's three phrases consists of 'enclosing heaven and earth' (函蓋乾坤句), 'cutting off the myriad streams' (截斷眾流句), and 'following the waves and pursuing the swells' (隨波逐浪句). The corpus explicitly distinguishes Yunmen's original words from the later three-part formulation. Yunmen addresses the assembly with 'enclosing heaven and earth; the eye weighs to the smallest measure; not touching the myriad conditions' (函蓋乾坤，目機銖兩，不涉萬緣), or with the variant 'not touching spring conditions' (不涉春緣). When no one answers, he supplies 'one arrowhead breaks three barriers' (一鏃破三關). Eye of Humans and Gods then says that his heir Deshan Yuanming split Yunmen's words into three phrases (後來德山圓明密禪師，遂離其語為三句) and names the set. Thereafter monks ask masters about each member in turn. This sense therefore records the triad conventionally named for Yunmen while retaining the corpus's statement that Deshan Yuanming made the three-part formulation.
Senses.Note: A genuinely distinct named triad, so the sense remains keyed to Yunmen. The text nevertheless says that Deshan Yuanming codified it from Yunmen's words (遂離其語為三句); it was not an utterance in which Yunmen himself listed the three later names. The constituent phrases also circulate independently: 'enclosing heaven and earth' (函蓋乾坤), 189 occurrences; 'cutting off the myriad streams' (截斷眾流), 370; 'following the waves and pursuing the swells' (隨波逐浪), 360.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師示眾云。函蓋乾坤。目機銖兩。不涉萬緣。作麼生承當。眾無對。自代云。一鏃破三關。後來德山圓明密禪師。遂離其語為三句。曰函蓋乾坤句。截斷眾流句。隨波逐浪句。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Eye of Humans and Gods (人天眼目), Huiyan Zhizhao reports Yunmen's source lines and states that Deshan Yuanming separated them into three phrases, naming all three members.

Occurrences.Kwic: 示眾云天中函蓋乾坤目機銖兩。不涉春緣。作麼生承當。代云。一鏃破三關。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Extensive Record of Chan Master Yunmen Kuangzhen (雲門匡真禪師廣錄), Yunmen Wenyan gives the source lines and the substitute answer 'one arrowhead breaks three barriers' from which the later triad was drawn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問。如何是函蓋乾坤句。師曰。天上有星皆拱北。曰。如何是截斷眾流句。師曰。大地坦
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Xichan Qin answers a monk's questions about the enclosing-heaven-and-earth and stream-cutting phrases in the completed triad.

Occurrences.Kwic: 三玄三要、四料簡、四賓主，洞山五位，雲門三句，百千法門無量妙義。若人揀得，許你具一隻眼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Recorded Sayings of Master Tianyin (天隱和尚語錄), Tianyin Yuanxiu quotes Yunmen's three phrases in a public list of named house devices and then records a response to that list.

Occurrences.Kwic: 進云：「雲門大師有三句，還許學人請益也無？」師云：「念得清楚來。」「如何是函蓋乾坤句？」師云：「日炤千門。」「如何是隨波逐浪句？」師云：「前谿水急。」「如何是截斷眾流句？」師云：「合取狗口。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Tian'an Sheng (天岸昇禪師語錄), Tian'an Sheng accepts a monk's request about Yunmen's three phrases and answers questions on each named member.

AlternateTargets: the first, second, and third phrases
Senses.Explanation: Linji's first, second, and third phrases (第一句 / 第二句 / 第三句), distinguished by rank. Linji says: attain it in the first phrase and you teach Buddhas and patriarchs; attain it in the second and you teach humans and gods; attain it in the third and you cannot even save yourself (若第一句中得，與祖佛為師；若第二句中得，與人天為師；若第三句中得，自救不了). Each phrase also receives a recorded answer. Asked 'What is the first phrase?' (如何是第一句), Linji replies that the seal of the three essentials opens with the vermilion mark narrow, and before deliberation is allowed host and guest are divided (三要印開朱點側，未容擬議主賓分). Eye of Humans and Gods collects the exchange, restates the ranking, and adds later comments. This is a different triad from the one named for Yunmen.
Senses.Note: A genuinely distinct Linji set. The compound 'Linji's three-phrase saying' (臨濟三句語) is raised in other houses. Linji's own record uses the ordinal names first, second, and third phrase; Eye of Humans and Gods titles the section 'three phrases' (三句).

Occurrences.Kwic: 若第一句中得，與祖佛為師；若第二句中得，與人天為師；若第三句中得，自救不了。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Linji Huizhao of Zhenzhou (鎮州臨濟慧照禪師語錄), Linji Yixuan gives the graded ranking of the first, second, and third phrases in a hall address.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：「如何是第一句？」師云：「三要印開朱點側，未容擬議主賓分。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Linji Huizhao of Zhenzhou (鎮州臨濟慧照禪師語錄), Linji Yixuan answers a monk's question about the first phrase; the second and third questions follow immediately.

Occurrences.Kwic: 第一句薦得。堪與佛祖為師。第二句薦得。堪與人天為師。第三句薦得。自救不了。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Eye of Humans and Gods (人天眼目), Huiyan Zhizhao restates Linji's ranking in the three-phrases section and then records comments by later masters.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師舉臨濟三句語問塔主。祇如塔中和尚得第幾句。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Compendium of the Five Lamps (五燈會元), Yunmen Wenyan explicitly raises Linji's three-phrase saying and asks the stupa keeper which phrase was attained.
